newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek farmers to lift roadblocks after 24 days.
newsitem.headline: Greek farmers to lift roadblocks after 24 days.

text.p: The main Greek farmers' committee voted on Sunday to lift a 24-day road blockade which has cut the country in two, caused transport chaos and cost the economy more than $100 million, committee members said.
The Thessaly farmers' committee, where the revolt began in November, called for all barricades to be lifted after a stormy marathon meeting, they said.
Reporters said many smaller roadblocks had come down already in the farmers' heartland in central Greece, stretching from Larissa to Volos on the mainland's eastern coast.

Four massive barricades, made up of thousands of tractors, remained around Larissa and traffic was still being stopped. Major blockades at Volos, about halfway between Athens and Greece's second city of Salonika in the north, were still in place but farmers said they would come down during the day.

An official statement on the decisions taken by the Thessaly farmers' committee was due during the day and was expected to spell out whether the road blockade was off or just suspended for Christmas holidays.

Committee members said the main question now was whether all farmers in the Larissa region would abide by the decision to lift the barricades and let millions of Greeks drive home for the Christmas holidays.
